data.title: Fade In / Out
data.tagline: Reveal or hide an element by changing its opacity
data.description: A fade is a simple transition between transparent and visible states. It works for overlays, messages, and content replacement, but opacity alone does not explain where an element came from. Combine it with small spatial motion only when that adds useful context.

use: Replace a small piece of content
Introduce a toast or status message
avoid: Fade critical content so slowly that work is delayed
Use opacity to hide an element that remains unexpectedly interactive
Combine large movement with every fade
Use repeated fades around text people are reading

lessonPractice.title: A toast only needs a light fade in and out, but after reaching zero opacity it still blocks a button underneath. How should it be fixed?

options.label: Transition opacity and remove hit testing, focus, and layout presence when exit completes
options.feedback: Fade owns the visual change, while interaction and final hidden state must synchronize so transparency stops blocking content.

options.label: Only set opacity to zero and keep the original layer and click area
options.feedback: Zero opacity does not remove an element; it may still cover buttons, occupy space, or receive keyboard focus.

options.label: Use pure fading for every overlay, including drawers that need to communicate a side origin
options.feedback: A toast suits light fading, but drawers may need movement to explain direction and should not share one universal effect.

data.agentPrompt: Give the toast a brief opacity fade and remove it from hit testing and focus order after exit, so it cannot block the page. Support reduced motion and test entering, visible, exiting, and removed states.
